From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sinha <priya@veridium.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Veridium Labs - capacity reservation & evaluation cadence

Priya —

Following our call this morning, attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for Veridium's evaluation-to-reserve path. The goal here is to lock a runway so you can hit production by end of Q1 without surprises on lead times or acceptance criteria. High-level asks below, full details in the spreadsheet: Veridium_MAP_v1.xlsx (attached).

Quick overview / asks:
- Confirm procurement milestone (internal PO/Finance OK) and expected date.
- Confirm preferred deployment: Redwood Dedicated (hosted reserved GPUs) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Lead times differ.
- Share the internal acceptance criteria for performance & security (latency SLO, token cost target, SOC2 evidence owner).

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) Eval kickoff & test plan agreement — this week
2) Pilot (2-week) on a small GPU pool — target mid-Oct
3) Tech QA & SOC2 evidence review — late Oct
4) Procurement & contract signature — Nov
5) Provisioning & canary rollout — Dec-Jan
6) Production cutover tranche 1 — Jan

Notes on lead times (prelim):
- Dedicated (reserved pool on Redwood): procurement to active pool ~8–12 weeks depending on tranche size and region.
- Private VPC / on-prem: 12–16 weeks (network, KMS, audit hooks add time).
- Short-term bridge: we can offer burst capacity for the pilot window to reduce blocker risk.

Ben and Marissa are on cc to align sizing and onboarding steps. I can iterate the MAP with your procurement date once you confirm.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

Mateo —

Thanks for the deck and the MAP draft. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Procurement is targeting a PO week on 2026-11-08, assuming the pilot shows runway. Could shift earlier if we get exec sign-off sooner.
- We are leaning toward Redwood Dedicated for the initial launch but want the option to move to an on-prem Private instance in H2.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for standard prompt mix, and embedding throughput of ~120 reqs/s with 100ms p95. We will share a formal doc.

I'll loop Ken from procurement to coordinate contracts and timing. Can Ben share an architecture sizing recommendation (pilot vs. production) so we can budget? Also, can you confirm what SOC2 evidence Redwood will provide vs. what we need to supply?

Priya Sinha

Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Veridium Labs - capacity reservation & evaluation cadence

Priya —

Nice, thanks. Ben — quick ask to include a short technical note in the MAP on pool sizing + recommended pilot config (we need a crisp recommendation Priya can take to finance).

To Priya — preliminary answers inline:
- Sizing (ballpark):
  * Pilot: 4x A100-80GB equivalent (or 8x A10s depending on model) configured as a small, reserved pool for a 2-week pilot. This supports concurrent eval and real-user load simulation with KV-cache warming.
  * Prod tranche 1: 12–16x A100-80GB equivalent for initial production (estimate based on expected concurrency & model cost targets).
  * H2 on-prem migration: we will produce a migration checklist and a sizing delta once you pick final hardware.
- Lead times: Dedicated: 8–12 weeks from signed contract to guaranteed reserved pool at production tranche size. Private/VPC: 12–16 weeks (networking + KMS onboarding). We'll run parallel pre-provisioning tasks to reduce the critical path.
- SOC2 evidence: Redwood provides the standard SOC2 report, rolling audit logs export, and we can provide architecture diagrams and configuration checklists. Anything marked 'customer-owned' (e.g., data retention policy enforcement inside your VPC) will need your engineering signoff.

I'll attach a short technical appendix and revised MAP after Ben's note.

-Mateo
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sinha <priya@veridium.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP: Veridium Labs - capacity reservation & evaluation cadence

Priya / Mateo —

Technical sizing note (concise):
- Model assumptions: eval will use an LLM load equivalent to about 3k tokens/req average, mix of generation and embedding calls. We recommend quantized 4-bit weights for production to reduce cost with minimal quality loss.
- Pilot config (recommended): 4x A100-80GB equiv, configured for continuous batching and prefix KV cache. Expected throughput: ~250 tokens/sec aggregate with p95 latency ~200ms for standard prompts.
- Production tranche 1: 12 GPUs for baseline 99qps embedding and 600 concurrent generation sessions with autoscaling headroom. Add +25% buffer for initial traffic spikes.
- Acceptance checks for pilot -> prod gate:
  1) Performance: p95 latency <= 250ms (see Priya's criteria) under load test profile.
  2) Cost: per-token cost meets agreed target (we'll provide token cost estimates by model/quantization).
  3) Security: SOC2 documentation received and network tests passed.
- Contingencies: If hardware lead time delays provisioning, we offer burst capacity and a short-term hosted routing policy to fall back to a smaller, higher-cost pool to meet production traffic.

I'll add these bullets into the MAP spreadsheet and add a tab for the acceptance test plan.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
